summary: Stale in-flight idempotency mapping after client crash + OAuth refresh results in orphaned downstream side-effects
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (DatumHealth) reports duplicate downstream webhook side-effects and orphaned jobs after a client process crash and automatic OAuth token refresh. Symptoms only appear when the client resumes a streaming session shortly after restart and the access token changes during the restart window.

Technical hypothesis in plain terms: the client persists an in-memory mapping of in-flight idempotency keys scoped to a session/token fingerprint. After a crash + token refresh the local mapping is reused but the server normalizes idempotency keys with a different token-derived prefix. This mismatch causes either (a) server to treat resumed requests as new (leading to duplicated webhook/tool invocations) or (b) server to mark pieces as acknowledged while the client thinks they are still pending, producing orphaned side-effects downstream.

Why this matters: DatumHealth runs high-value side-effects (billing events, external state changes) from SDK-driven function calls. Duplicate or orphaned side-effects violate their data consistency and regulatory audit requirements for patient-facing workflows.
impact: Customer reports ~6 duplicated webhook callbacks over the last 48 hours across 3 separate restarts. Each duplicate triggered an idempotent-safety guard at their downstream system, but two resulted in repeated billing line-items. Customer considers this a blocking behaviour for production use until a robust mitigation is in place.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a long-running streaming session that issues function/tool calls with an application-level idempotency header (X-RW-Client-Idemp or equivalent).
Persist the in-flight idempotency map on disk in client process between sends (this matches customer SDK behavior for quick restarts).
Trigger a client crash (SIGKILL) while there are pending function calls not yet fully confirmed by the webhook proxy.
Allow the client to restart: on start the client obtains a fresh OAuth access token from the identity provider (short window refresh).
Resume the streaming session using the persisted in-flight mapping but the new access token; resume connection to the same API endpoint and re-send pending frames.
Observe the webhook endpoints for duplicate invocations and check server-side idempotency store for key normalization mismatch.
expected_behavior: After restart+refresh, resumed requests should be matched to prior in-flight entries and treated as the same logical operation (no duplicate webhook invocations). Server-side idempotency lookup should not rely on ephemeral token-derived prefixes that change across refreshes, or the SDK should rotate persisted mappings when token identity changes.
actual_behavior: Server treated resumed frames as fresh in some runs and as already-acked in others; downstream webhooks received duplicates or partial/stranded state. The customer observed both duplicate billing events and orphaned 'pending' jobs left in their queue with no matching confirmation. Logs show the idemp key presented by the client does not normalize to the same server-side canonical key after token refresh.
logs:
snippets:
- client stdout (on restart): 'restoring in-flight map (N=3), new access_token received (len=123)'.
- api-gateway: 'idempotency_lookup miss: key=f17e4a... token_prefix=tok_v2'
- webhook-proxy: 'delivered actionId=abcd-1234 status=200 (second_delivery)'.
- downstream system: 'billing line item created: charge_id=chg_45678 (duplicate of chg_45679)'.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support (Priya): confirmed customer reproducer and collected network traces. Observed token fingerprint (first 8 chars of token hash) differs pre- and post-crash. Server idempotency store currently normalizes keys as 'token_fingerprint:idempotency_key'. That design assumption breaks on token refresh.

SRE notes (Liam): checked gateway logs and rate-limiter traces — no throttling involved. Webhook proxy shows duplicate delivery windows within seconds of resume. Serving runtime trace shows request handled on the same backend host; backend respects idempotency store result.

SDK team (R&D): local persistence of in-flight map currently does not include a canonical client identity separate from access token. Suggest two mitigation approaches: (1) server-side: relax normalization to ignore token prefix when idempotency metadata contains a stable client_id header, or (2) client-side: bind persisted mapping to a stable client id and rotate mapping on token change.

We have a low-risk repro and a proposed workaround to forward to customer while engineering implements a fix.
comments: Priya Shah (Support) - 2026-03-10: Collected detailed reproducer from DatumHealth and validated duplicate webhook deliveries in their logs. Asked for a minimal repro that can be run in our infra.

DatumHealth (Customer) - 2026-03-10: Provided a dockerized reproducer and noted they persist in-flight map to disk for fast restarts (k8s pod restarts). Confirmed duplicates were observed immediately after restart when token rotated.

Liam O'Connor (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed server-side idempotency key normalization includes token fingerprint. Logged a short-term mitigation: allow an 'X-RW-Client-Id' header to override token-based scoping for idempotency lookups when present.

Anika Bose (SDK) - 2026-03-12: Drafted SDK patch to include stable client_id in persisted map and to reject restoring in-flight entries if oauth token fingerprint differs unless client_id matches. Preparing tests and PR.
Priya Shah (Support) - 2026-03-12: Informed customer of mitigation path and requested they opt-in to new header override for a pilot.
resolution:
Workaround applied: Support enabled server-side acceptance of 'X-RW-Client-Id' for idempotency scoping for the affected customer (DatumHealth) in prod-us-east. This prevents token-refresh-based mismatches when the client persists a stable client_id.

Engineering plan: SDK patch (PR #2213) will include stable client_id persistence and a sanity check on token fingerprint during restore; if mismatch and no stable client_id present, SDK will refuse to auto-resume in-flight entries. Server follow-up: consider migrating idempotency keys to a canonical client identifier instead of token-derived prefixes.

Follow-ups: 1) SDK team to land PR and publish patch notes; 2) SRE to monitor for duplicate webhook incidents for 72 hours post-change; 3) CS to run audit with DatumHealth to reconcile affected billing items (finance involvement).
next_steps: Ship SDK patch and new minor release (agent-sdk v1.8.4) and publish migration guidance.
SRE to roll out server-side header override to additional customers only by request and schedule a config toggle for safe rollback.
Customer success to coordinate billing reconciliation with DatumHealth finance team.
Postmortem/Confluence page to be updated with recommended best practices for persisted in-flight state and token churn.
